referencesAre: Unmodified upstream armor atlases, study only; no upstream pixels used in production.
wardweave: Create a Minecraft magic ARMOR TEXTURE source study for Wardweave robes, inspired by the readable pixels and rich garment construction of the attached Electroblob wizard and sage ARMOR atlases. Independently create a new design. This is cloth magic armor: a structured high collar, layered lapels, a small sapphire/silver ward clasp, substantial dark slate cuffs, a narrow leather belt, and a split knee-length coat with silver-edged front opening. NOT a cape, not a poncho, no back flap, no hat, no boots, no character. The entire torso and sleeves must have a designed wizard outfit identity, not a plain shirt with accessory added. Crucial: draw THREE perfectly flat rectangular UV FACE STUDIES on a plain medium warm gray background: LEFT front of torso-and-lower-robe, 8 logical pixels wide by 20 logical pixels high; CENTER back of torso-and-lower-robe, also 8x20; RIGHT front sleeve, 4x12. All three share exactly the same logical pixel size and integer square grid. Show whole garment face in each rectangle with no margins inside it. Front/back upper 12 rows are torso, next 8 are lower coat; belt at rows 10-11, coat slit in bottom 8 rows. Sleeve top 3 rows are dark slate structured shoulder, bottom 3 are folded charcoal cuffs with silver seam. Use a tiny Minecraft-style palette: dyeable main cloth is PURE NEUTRAL GRAYS (155,155,155 / 185,185,185 / 215,215,215), fixed dark slate/charcoal trim at 40-80, limited desaturated silverblue edges and a two-pixel sapphire clasp. Rich but broad folded fabric shadows, crisp single logical pixels, no dithering, no little noisy speckles, no fine details below logical grid. Keep at least 60% main cloth neutral and dyeable. The BACK is a fitted continuous jacket body with shaped shoulder seams and a belt, not a cape. Logical pixels enlarged as sharp perfectly flat squares. Output no lettering, labels, lighting effects, 3D, outlines around rectangles, or decorative sheet framing. Make it look like an excellent actual Minecraft wizard armor texture.
